newsitem.title: POLAND: Optimus sees operating profit rising.
newsitem.headline: Optimus sees operating profit rising.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA should better last year's 35.9-million-zloty operating profit this year despite a fall in first-quarter operating returns due to investment and tariff costs, Optimus' financial head said.

Stefan Mroczek told a news conference on Monday that Optimus' first quarter operating profit shrank to 2.9 million zlotys from 6.2 million in part because of heightened investment in non-computer areas such as the Internet.
"We're training 50 new employees," Moczek said, adding that the firm was also stung by this year's new tariff on imported computer components, which he sees being removed later this year.

Mroczek said Optimus lifted first quarter net profit to 10.1 million zlotys from 2.7 million, helped by financial operations such as liquidating reserves linked with its $30 million convertible bond programme.
Optimus expects to earn 30 million zlotys this year, 43.2 million zlotys consolidated.

Mroczek said 1997 consolidated profit would be boosted through sales by cash register subsidiary Optimus IC, which parent company treasurer Janusz Topolski said should maintain its 27-30 percent market share this year.
He said about 120,000 cash registers had been sold by firms operating in Poland in 1995-1996 and that the number should rise to 500,000 by the end of 1998.
Mroczek also said Optimus was mulling applications of chip card technology, which the firm could sell to the banking and security industries.
